The ninth floor of the Miami-Dade pretrial detention facility is dubbed the 'forgotten floor'.

Judges like Steven Leifman advocate for changing the treatment of mentally ill patients in jails.
200 years ago, people considered 'lunatics' were locked up in jails even if they had no charges against them.
Over the years, public outcry moved the mentally ill out of jails and into hospitals, but many of these hospitals were shut down.
Many of the mentally ill patients end up on the streets or become homeless without receiving treatment.
Starting in 2008, many inmates who would otherwise be brought to the 'forgotten floor' will instead be sent to a new mental health facility, marking a step toward long-term treatment.
